description: Tutorial lesson T2 (Musterin' da Boyz), the deploy_grots step ('GROTS IN A MOB!') on a GAMEPAD: proves the lesson's pad prompt teaches the D-pad route to the Tight formation instead of telling the player to glide the virtual cursor onto the Tight button. The boot up to deploy_grots is mirrored from tut_t2_musterin (which owns that path, including the rotate_wagon / nudge_wagon / confirm_wagon steps) and is driven mouse+keyboard; claim_pad() then flips the card to its pad body with NO unit picked yet, and that body is asserted to name the Gretchin plus BOTH bumper chips (reported: the step said to pick the Gretchin without saying which button switches unit; naming only RB then left a player reaching for LB - which works identically - with no confirmation) before LB actually starts placing them. Pins WHY the D-pad up press is needed: the Gretchin have two model profiles (Runtherd + Grots), so the card carries two selector rows and the marker starts on Select Model Type - left/right there would cycle the model type, not the formation. D-pad up moves the marker to Deploy Formation (the label gains its marker), then D-pad right twice steps Single -> Spread -> Tight and the Tight toggle syncs. Finishes the step exactly as the prompt says: A warps the cursor, glide + A lays each Tight rank, Menu confirms -> Gretchin DEPLOYED and the lesson advances to first_turn_roll.

steps.comment: OptionButton popup menus are native Windows - select+emit is the dropdown escape hatch
the Formations panel is a modal embedded Window - synthetic root-viewport clicks cannot reach its controls; setting button_pressed emits toggled exactly like a click
tie tolerance: press the roll button if still up, else the A DEAD HEAT re-roll button; no-op when neither exists
park the pointer where the wagon will go so the ghost renders on the board - the rotation has to be VISIBLE in the screenshots below, not just readable off the controller

steps.script:
var dc = tree.root.get_node("Main").deployment_controller
if dc.ghost_sprite == null:
	return "NO_GHOST"
return abs(wrapf(dc.ghost_sprite.get_base_rotation() - BoardState.get_default_facing_for_player(1), -PI, PI)) < 0.001
steps.comment: the wagon ghost starts at the default enemy-facing, so the rotate step cannot be already-done on entry
picking the wagon up is NOT enough - the step still waits for a real turn
Confirm is gated until the wagon is turned - otherwise a player could deploy it flat and strand the step with no ghost left to rotate
rotate_right = +15 degrees a tap, so six taps is a quarter turn

steps.script:
var dc = tree.root.get_node("Main").deployment_controller
var want = BoardState.get_default_facing_for_player(1) + PI / 2.0
return abs(wrapf(dc.ghost_sprite.get_base_rotation() - want, -PI, PI)) < 0.02

steps.comment: turning the ghost is what advances the step
placing the wagon now advances to the nudge step, not straight to Confirm
shift+click the placed wagon to pick it back up - the gesture this step teaches
drop 1.5in sideways: the wagon was turned 90deg so its long axis is horizontal, and the zone's y<=12in step sits just below

steps.script:
var m = GameState.get_unit("U_BATTLEWAGON_T").models[0]
var want = BoardState.get_default_facing_for_player(1) + PI / 2.0
return abs(wrapf(float(m.get("rotation", 0.0)) - want, -PI, PI)) < 0.02
steps.comment: the turn the tutorial taught actually lands on the deployed wagon, not just on the ghost

flip the card to its PAD body while NO unit has been picked yet - the state the reported player was stuck in. Uses the claim_pad() seam rather than a stick nudge on purpose: a real axis event drags the virtual cursor (and edge-pushes the camera), which desynced the absolute pad_cursor_glide placements later in this scenario.
nothing is being deployed yet - the prompt asserted next has to TELL the player how to pick the Gretchin, not assume they already did

REGRESSION GUARD (reported: 'it says pick the Gretchin but never says how'): the pad prompt names the Gretchin AND BOTH bumper chips. LB and RB both switch unit (PadRouter's bumper-only rule) and the Gretchin are the last unit left, so a prompt naming only one of them under-describes the control. Reads the glyph text off GlyphDB rather than hardcoding 'RB'/'LB' so a controller remap keeps the assertion honest.
LB is the deployment hint bar's Prev Unit - the Gretchin are the only unit left, so the bumper the prompt just taught starts their placement
the rendered pad prompt teaches the D-pad ({dpad} -> the ✚ chip) and no longer tells the player to glide the cursor onto the Tight button
the Gretchin carry two model profiles (Runtherd + Grots), so the card has two selector rows
WHY the prompt starts with D-pad ▲: the marker starts on Select Model Type, so ◀ ▶ here would cycle the model type, not the formation
D-pad ▲ - slide the ▶ marker onto the Deploy Formation row
the on-card marker the prompt names is really there
D-pad ▶ (1 of 2) - Single -> Spread
D-pad ▶ (2 of 2) - Spread -> Tight
the D-pad drove the on-screen toggle row too, not just the controller's internal mode
A warps the virtual cursor over the placement area
Tight lays a whole rank of 5 per press - the payoff the step is teaching
the Runtherd
Menu = Confirm, exactly as the prompt now says
step 6 completed end-to-end on pad input only
